completion_scope.headward_scope: The mapped southern dashed drainage and adjoining feeder junctions were read from the original 250k overview and headwater detail. The initial small upland segment is handled at ordinary headwater-corridor scale, without requiring exact first-channel or spring-point agreement. The partly blank 100k image is supplementary and does not leave a gap in the already readable 250k corridor.
completion_scope.lake_and_wetland_scope: The route passes neighboring upland lagoons without treating their names as channel names, follows low channel and wetland belts near Bajo de la Mora and Laguna Arancibia, and enters the Menucos and Trapalcó saline-basin sequence. The mapped connection between the saline depressions is read explicitly, rather than inferred from basin membership or model connectivity.
material_junctions_inspected: Southern feeder and side drainage around Cerro Encayapau and San Antonio del Cuy
Eastern-foot drainage at Barda Anocibar and the El Cuy junction setting, including the distinct western San Salvador corridor
La Punta and Bajo de la Mora convergence setting
Currumil–Soledad lowland and the El Salado continuation near Curacó
El Salado and the distinct Caita Co southern tributary convergence
Western entry into Salitral Bajo de Menucos and its southeastern outlet-channel corridor
Puesto Las Salinas junctions and northwestern entry to Salinas de Trapalcó
completion_scope.actual_terminal_setting: The selected endpoint lies inside the mapped northern/eastern part of Salinas de Trapalcó. This is an inland saline receiving depression, not a Río Negro or ocean outlet. The model does not continue through every lagoon south of the salinas.
completion_scope.gap_character: No material source-connection gap remains. White bands in the detailed terminal export are covered by the already acquired overview, which explicitly depicts the same channels and junctions. The naming hold concerns the scope and feature type of the available names.

records.region: Northern Patagonia, Argentina; El Cuy–Soledad–El Salado–Menucos drainage to Salinas de Trapalcó.
records.candidate_name_role: Completed geographic correspondence of the selected drainage from the El Cuy uplands through the Soledad and El Salado canyon corridors to the Menucos and Trapalcó saline depressions. Printed canyon names and receiving-salina names are component identities; no inspected source establishes a representative river-system hydronym for this selected chain.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: Full geographic correspondence is complete, but the inspected names identify individual canyon corridors and saline receivers rather than a representative river-system hydronym. The absence of a uniform scalar name alone is not the reason for this hold.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected route follows a mapped dashed-channel feeder from the southern El Cuy uplands past the Cerro Encayapau and San Antonio del Cuy setting, turns north along the eastern foot of Altiplanicie del Cuy and Barda Anocibar, and continues through El Cuy and La Punta into Bajo de la Mora. It then follows the Currumil and Cañadón Soledad lowland toward the Cañadón El Salado corridor, continues east past Curacó and Loma La Jarancha, enters the Caita Co convergence and Salitral Bajo de Menucos, and follows the southeastern saline-channel connection by Puesto Las Salinas into Salinas de Trapalcó. The endpoint lies within the mapped salinas. All material connections are supported at ordinary corridor scale. Canyon, settlement and salt-basin labels are distinguished from an unestablished representative river hydronym.
records.supported_name_scope: Completed geographic correspondence of the selected drainage from the El Cuy uplands through the Soledad and El Salado canyon corridors to the Menucos and Trapalcó saline depressions. Printed canyon names and receiving-salina names are component identities; no inspected source establishes a representative river-system hydronym for this selected chain.

component_scope_limits: This is not a hold merely because every segment lacks one uniform scalar name. Full geographic correspondence has been completed, but the inspected names identify individual canyons and saline receivers rather than establishing a representative named river system.
Cañadón Soledad and Cañadón El Salado are printed canyon-corridor labels. Their geographic correspondence is supported, while their use as river-system hydronyms remains unestablished.
The unnamed southern feeder is not renamed after nearby San Salvador, Grande de El Cuy, Chico de El Cuy, a settlement, or a lagoon.
Historical dashed-channel and salt-flat depiction does not establish present flow, permanence, water level or modern hydraulic behavior.
Formal registry status and Korean name are unverified; no product naming or automatic application is authorized by this finding.

records.completion_scope: The full selected geography is read at ordinary corridor scale: the national original covers the northern opening and overlaps the 2007 detailed sheet at its 62°30′N edge; that sheet covers the southern interior, lower nunatak/glacier-margin bends and actual inner-fjord ending. This is geographic correspondence, not a surveyed river trace or current ice-front determination.
records.region: Southern Greenland; Inland Ice, Eqalorutsit Kangillit Sermiat and inner Nordre Sermilik west of Johan Dahl Land.
records.candidate_name_role: No supported representative natural-river identity. Glacier, land and receiving-fjord names identify local geographic context only.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The selected route occupies mapped southern Inland Ice, continues into an ice-and-nunatak margin corridor, and ends in the Eqalorutsit Kangillit Sermiat/inner Nordre Sermilik setting. The original maps establish this geography but do not establish a representative natural-river identity for the complete modeled route.
records.geographic_disambiguation: This selection's southern ending is the Eqalorutsit Kangillit Sermiat/inner Nordre Sermilik setting. Qooqqup Sermia and Qooroq lie in a separate corridor to the east of Johan Dahl Land. Names associated with earlier selections, including Søndre Qipisaqqu Bræ and the separate western Sermilik setting, are not transferred to this object.

completion_scope.headward_scope: The detailed 1:100,000 view resolves the selected initial mountain valley and its northward channel, the eastward piedmont turn, and the southeast intermittent drainage through the Balde del Rosario setting. The coarser 1:250,000 view alone was insufficiently explicit for parts of this headward channel; the detailed map was actually inspected.
material_junctions_inspected: Mountain feeder and north-facing piedmont drainage below Mogote de Arriba/Abajo
Balde del Rosario and San Antonio-side alluvial drainage in the Loma del Puesto–Loma Negra setting
Médano Colorado–Barreal Atravesado corridor and Usno-side drainage toward Colonia Los Valencianos/Baldes del Norte
Northern approach meeting the Río del Valle corridor east of San Agustín, with the western Río del Valle/reservoir branch distinguished
Las Tumanas and Astica-side distributary/fan drainage meeting the lower valley setting
Barreal Colorado/Chucuma lower depression chain and its continuation to the Mascasín salina margin
completion_scope.lake_reservoir_scope: Dique/Embalse San Agustín is visible on the western Río del Valle branch by the town. The selected route approaches from the north and enters the downstream valley east of it; the selected object is not claimed to cross that reservoir. No other selected lake or reservoir crossing is established. The terminal salina is a separate land/water-surface feature, not a river reach to be renamed.
completion_scope.actual_terminal_setting: The selected terminus is inside the mapped Salinas de Mascasín depression, south of the Marayes–Mascasín road/rail crossing and east of the Pampa del Gigantillo setting. It is not an ocean mouth, and no onward surface outlet is established.
completion_scope.lower_connection_basis: The detailed 1:100,000 map depicts the selected lower route through the elongated Barreal de Chucuma and adjoining dry-depression chain leading into the mapped salinas. The plan independently states that exceptionally large floods continue east and south to Salinas de Mascasín. At ordinary corridor scale these complementary observations establish the seasonal land/water continuation; they do not establish year-round flow or every individual distributary junction.
completion_scope.completion_boundary: Completed representative-system correspondence at ordinary component/corridor scale. Exact spring, channel-bank, barreal margin, salina shoreline, individual flood-distributary and mouth-point agreement is neither required nor claimed. The two unavailable optional geological sheets leave no unresolved geographic gap after the actual IGN detailed-map reading.

records.region: San Juan and La Rioja setting, Argentina; northern mountain/alluvial feeder, Río del Valle and seasonal barreal continuation to Salinas de Mascasín.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative name of the receiving named river corridor east of San Agustín de Valle Fértil and its exceptional-flood continuation toward Salinas de Mascasín. The selected headward mountain feeder, northern alluvial/barreal passages and salina interior are not assigned this name individually.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected route begins in an unnamed north-draining mountain channel on the eastern Sierra de Valle Fértil near the Campo Grande–Agua de la Laguna setting. It turns east below Mogote de Arriba and then southeast through the Balde del Rosario, Loma Negra and Médano Colorado alluvial corridors. It follows the Barreal Atravesado/Usno-side lowland into the Río del Valle corridor east of San Agustín. Downstream it follows the east-then-south valley and the lower barreal chain, including Barreal de Chucuma, to the Salinas de Mascasín depression. Original historical 100k and 250k cartography supports all generalized components. The official departmental plan explains that the river usually infiltrates near San Agustín and reaches the salinas only during exceptional floods. This is a mixed mountain-channel, intermittent alluvial and terminal-salina system, not a claim of permanent surface continuity or one uniform hydronym.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative name of the receiving named river corridor east of San Agustín de Valle Fértil and its exceptional-flood continuation toward Salinas de Mascasín. The selected headward mountain feeder, northern alluvial/barreal passages and salina interior are not assigned this name individually.

completion_scope.cartographic_basis: Holm Figure 3.1 and WSA Figure 1 were visually inspected from successfully acquired original PDFs. The maps provide continuous ordinary-corridor coverage. Reservoir-specific connections are also supported by the WSA's explicit prose; detailed reservoir shorelines are not claimed.
material_junctions_inspected: Southern western headward corridor, eastward reach south of Mankota, and northward Wood River turn
Wood River through the Summercove impoundment setting, with its on-river relationship established by WSA prose
Southern tributary junction setting and continuation through Thomson Lake/Lafleche Dam
Gravelbourg–Shamrock lower corridor and the western tributary arrivals
Lower Wood River division between the northward Chaplin diversion and the eastward Old Wives Lake route
Western lake entry and the selected continuation into Old Wives Lake
completion_scope.terminal_setting: The actual selected terminal is in the Old Wives Lake basin/waterbody setting, beyond the western river-entry reach. It is not the Chaplin diversion or a downstream outlet from Old Wives Lake.
completion_scope.precision_limit: Generalized corridor and component correspondence only. No precise bank, dam-axis, mouth vertex, reservoir boundary or present-day wet shoreline is asserted. This is not a claim of perennial through-flow.

records.region: Southern Saskatchewan, Canada; Wood River, Summercove/Thomson impoundment links and Old Wives Lake terminal.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative identity of the selected Wood River system, including its impounded passages and continuation into the terminal Old Wives Lake setting; not a uniform hydronym for every modeled segment.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The independently acquired WSA watershed plan and Holm field-study thesis support Wood River as the representative identity. Their maps trace the southern headward corridor below Mankota, its eastward bend and northward continuation through the Thomson Lake–Gravelbourg corridor, then the northeastern approach to Old Wives Lake. The selected route continues into that terminal lake setting. Reservoir and terminal-lake names remain distinct from the river name.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity of the selected Wood River system, including its impounded passages and continuation into the terminal Old Wives Lake setting; not a uniform hydronym for every modeled segment.

source_name_scope.supported_name_scope: Wood River is supported as a representative river-system identity by a continuous mapped trunk and explicitly described upstream-to-terminal drainage. The support does not come from the bounding box or a neighboring name label.
source_name_scope.scope_limit: The river hydronym is not transferred to the reservoir surfaces, terminal lake interior, tributaries or engineered Chaplin diversion. No separate formal name for every initial feeder or legal extent of Wood River has been established. These limits do not create a missing physical connector or prevent a representative identity.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
